clue.text: Poor performers ramble on Sunday

definitions.note: plural noun: weak players in sport

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length

explanation.surface: Someone complains that weak performers keep droning on every Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sporting slang a 'rabbit' is a poor player, especially a hopeless batsman in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting slang calls a feeble player, notably a tail-end cricket batsman, a rabbit.

clue.text: Compensation for heartlessly rude habit

indicators.note: heartlessly means the centre of the word rude is taken out

parts.note: a habit is a garment, a form of dress

explanation.surface: Someone seeks damages for a monk's offensively crude robe.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is reparation or remedy for a wrong suffered.

clue.text: Herring or puffer fish?

definitions.meaning: playfully, a thing that bloats or puffs up

explanation.definitionFit: A kipper-like smoked herring is called a bloater; read literally, the word means something that swells up or puffs.

clue.text: Religion that's primarily spread in mail order

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the rearranged word
order means the letters of mail are put into a new order
primarily picks out the first letter of spread

explanation.surface: A faith is said to have grown mainly through mail-order catalogues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' turns MAIL into ILAM, and 'in' places S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith of Muslims.

clue.text: Some drugs that save diets going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters of save and diets are jumbled

explanation.surface: Certain medicines rescue dieters when their regime fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedatives are calming medications that induce sleep or relaxation.

clue.text: Gift wrapping a ship's instrument

indicators.note: the gift is wrapped round, so its letters enclose the other pieces

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing
SS stands for steamship, as in ship names

explanation.surface: A present has been wrapped around something belonging to a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassoon is a low-pitched woodwind instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: Public transport accepts very loud enthusiastic fans

indicators.note: the bus accepts the other letters, taking them inside

parts.note: a bus is public transport
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A bus lets on a noisy crowd of eager supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffs are devotees or keen followers of a pursuit.

clue.text: Telephone equipment needed by oddly sick walker

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of sick

parts.note: a rambler is a hiker or country walker

explanation.surface: A poorly hiker needs some phone kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrambler is a device that encodes phone signals so eavesdroppers cannot understand them.

clue.text: Go too far in maiden race

parts.note: a maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored
a run is a race

explanation.surface: A young woman overshoots in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a girl; in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to exceed a limit, such as a time slot.

clue.text: The lunatic needs a beanbag

parts.note: bean and nut are both slang for the head, and a nut is also a seed like a bean
a case is a bag, as in a suitcase

explanation.surface: A madman must have his beanbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcase is informal slang for a crazy person.

clue.text: Made silly drawings — a doddle curiously, nothing in it

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the rearranged word, which 'it' points back to
curiously signals that the letters of doddle are arranged in an odd new way

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Doodling is apparently easy, a doddle with nothing to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' turns DODDLE into DODLED, and 'in it' puts O inside that: DO+O+DLED. A 'doddle' is British slang for an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: To doodle is to scribble idle sketches, which is the past tense here.

clue.text: Fresh offer — it is fine

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new version, so the letters of offer and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new offer is put forward and declared to be fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A forfeit is a penalty paid for a wrongdoing, just as a fine is.

clue.text: Reckons that grounds cover one mile

indicators.note: the grounds cover, so they surround the other letters

parts.note: estates are landed grounds round a big house
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that the grounds stretch over a mile.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to reckon or calculate roughly.

clue.text: The girl to spoil first class return!

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: return means the letters for first class are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the figure 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone is warned not to spoil a girl's first-class trip back.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a girl's given name, the sort of example crosswords often use.

clue.text: Take off in gear

explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to take off clothes; a team's strip is its matching kit or outfit.

clue.text: Kept jam on top of display

parts.note: a preserve is a jam

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of display in a down clue

explanation.surface: Jam was saved on top of a shop display.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserved means maintained or saved from decay.

clue.text: Self appointed policeman leaving it to be resolved

indicators.note: resolved here means broken down and reworked, so the letters of leaving and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A volunteer lawman walks off, leaving the matter for others to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante takes on law enforcement without any official authority.

clue.text: Sponsor Hermes, perhaps even a hospital department

parts.note: Hermes is an example of a Greek god
par means even, level
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A backer is likened to Hermes, even to a hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: At a baptism a godparent acts as sponsor for the child.

clue.text: I am in a hurry and favourably influenced

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
pressed for time means in a hurry

explanation.surface: Someone is rushed but has been won over all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impressed is to feel admiration after being affected by something.

clue.text: A dip is nice, but offered up with little taste

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the run is read from the bottom upwards
offered here means the letters are presented within the words dip is nice

explanation.surface: A dip is pleasant, but the one served up is bland.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'dip is ni' backwards: 'offered' shows the run, 'up' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food lacks flavour, which is having little taste.

clue.text: One who paces restlessly around the front of the ship put out at alert

parts.note: the prow is the bow of a ship

indicators.note: put out means the word at is removed from alert

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sentry on alert stalks about near the bow of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out at alert' takes AT out of ALERT, leaving LER.
explanation.definitionFit: A prowler moves about stealthily, often with ill intent.

clue.text: Engineers in favour of traditional style, but new

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: Engineers back a classic look that is nonetheless freshly made.
explanation.definitionFit: Repro furniture is a modern reproduction made in a period manner.

clue.text: A game of bridge?

explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon is a card game like blackjack; a pontoon bridge rests on floating supports.

clue.text: Secretive people often found in bed

definitions.meaning: those who keep things shut tight

explanation.definitionFit: Close-mouthed people are likened to tightly shut shellfish, and these shellfish grow on seabed beds.

clue.text: Scratch team's total

explanation.definitionFit: To score is to mark a surface with a line; the score is the points a side has amassed.

clue.text: Banners announcing ladies' hen gathering

indicators.note: a gathering brings things together in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Big signs proclaim a ladies' hen party.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a British pre-wedding celebration for the bride and her friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Banner headlines run across a newspaper's front page in large print.

clue.text: Took on staff of better quality, we hear, and ultimately profited

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: higher means of better quality

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of profited

explanation.surface: A firm recruited better staff and finally made money.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire is to employ, so hired means took on workers.

clue.text: £2 should cover primate collar

indicators.note: the two letters cover the other piece by going either side of it

parts.note: the pound sign comes from L for libra, so two of them give two Ls
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Two pounds ought to pay for a monkey's collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded-back part of a coat collar.

clue.text: China, say, making a fuss

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china means pal
to aver is to state or say firmly

explanation.surface: Someone claims their china is causing an upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain or the country; it is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: A palaver is a tiresome bother or commotion over something minor.

clue.text: Examine former political leader's traditional knowledge

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lore is knowledge handed down by tradition

explanation.surface: Someone studies an ex-party leader's store of old wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore a subject is to investigate it thoroughly.

clue.text: Mocked the act having got in free

indicators.note: having got in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an act
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A performance was jeered after its cast slipped in without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to ridicule or scoff at.

clue.text: Story taken by the national theatre may point to special gifts

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the National Theatre in London
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A tale staged by the National may show off remarkable abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Talents are natural abilities or aptitudes.
